entry.title: Stellar evolution and axion-like particles: new constraints and hints from globular clusters in the GAIA DR3 data
entry.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are hypothetical pseudoscalar bosons, natural in extensions of the Standard Model. Their interactions with ordinary matter and radiation are suppressed, making it challenging to detect them in laboratory experiments. However, these particles, produced within stellar interiors, can provide an additional mechanism for energy loss, potentially influencing stellar evolution. Prominent methods for searching for such effects involve measuring the properties of red giants and helium-burning stars in globular clusters (GCs). Here we use published catalogs of stars selected as members of seven GCs on the basis of parallaxes and proper motions measured by Gaia (Data Release 3). Making use of previously derived theoretical relations and the new data, we find the upper limit on the ALP-electron coupling, g_{ae}<1.3*10^{-13} (95% CL), and an indication (2.6 sigma) to nonzero ALP-photon coupling, g_{aγ}=(6.6+1.3-1.8)*10^{-11} GeV^{-1}. Given the precision of contemporary observational data, it is imperative to refine ALP constraints through more sophisticated analyses, which will be explored in detail elsewhere.

entry.title: Decoupling of large-scale, adiabatic inflationary perturbations from enhanced small-scale modes at one-loop
entry.summary: We reconsider back-reaction from large amplitude, short-scale perturbations onto a long wavelength adiabatic mode. In a loop expansion of the long-mode power spectrum, this back-reaction appears first at 1-loop. Due to the separation between the long and short scales, the separate universe method provides a simple and efficient framework for this computation. In this paper, building on our earlier work, we employ a $δN$ formula for the long mode, which captures the effect of short scales. We show that back-reaction at 1-loop is due to either (i) non-linearity of the $δN$ formula, or (ii) 1-loop corrections to the initial conditions. We argue that contributions of type (ii) cannot themselves be described within the separate universe framework, but their properties can be constrained using soft theorems and a ''multi-point propagator'' expansion. When applied to a band of enhanced short-scale perturbations that crossed the horizon during inflation, our result shows that the loop correction decouples from their detailed properties. Furthermore, the back-reaction we obtain is scale-invariant. Its magnitude is model-dependent, but is degenerate with effects from modes that were still sub-horizon at the end of inflation. In this scenario (but not necessarily in all scenarios), we conclude that the effect is not observable.

entry.title: Learning to stabilize nonequilibrium phases of matter with active feedback using partial information
entry.summary: Recent advances in quantum computing experiments have enabled new pathways for feedback control. Here, we investigate the role of information in interactive quantum many-body dynamics to engineer out-of-equilibrium phases of matter. To this end, we train reinforcement learning agents to prevent entanglement spreading in (1+1)-dimensional stabilizer circuits with up to 128 qubits. We find that, above an information threshold, agents learn stochastic near-optimal strategies that prevent the system from reaching volume-law entangled states and instead stabilize area-law scaling. These strategies rely on bottlenecks that divide the system and cap the entanglement in the steady state. Crucially, learned strategies are inherently out of equilibrium, require real-time active feedback, and could not be reproduced by simple human-designed control rules. This work establishes the foundations for information-driven individual control of many interacting quantum degrees of freedom, demonstrating the capabilities of reinforcement learning to stabilize and uncover novel critical properties of many-body nonequilibrium steady states.

entry.title: 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$: matching $A(k)$ in ABJM free energy
entry.summary: The function $A(k)$ appearing in the large $N$ expansion of free energy of ABJM theory on $S^3$ is known exactly from localization. An earlier calculation of the 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, based on the standard KK spectrum on $S^7$, did not reproduce it. We identify a missing 1-loop supergravity contribution as that of the 3-form field fluctuations built from square-integrable harmonic 2-forms on Euclidean $\mathrm{AdS}_4$ tensored with $S^7$ modes, which are not captured by the KK spectrum. Adding it to the KK tower contribution expressed in terms of superconformal characters and applying the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ projection, the total expression simplifies, and its evaluation in a zeta-function prescription reproduces the expression for $A(k)$. We also apply a similar approach to the 3d ADHM theory whose M-theory dual is the orbifold $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_p$, which has singularity along the fixed locus $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^3$, supporting a 7d $SU(p)$ vector multiplet. Adding the localized KK modes of this multiplet to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-projected supergravity spectrum gives a 1-loop free energy that reproduces the ADHM localization counterpart of $A(k)$.

entry.title: Engineering many-body tunneling dynamics of one-dimensional bosons with finite-core power-law interactions
entry.summary: We investigate the many-body dynamics of a one-dimensional Bose-Josephson junction of ultracold bosons in a box-like potential with a central barrier, interacting via finite-core power-law interactions $V_α(r)=g/(r^α+d^α)$, where $d$ sets the short-distance scale and $α$ controls the spatial dependence. Using the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method for bosons (MCTDHB), we explore how the interaction profile and strength, barrier, and initial population imbalance shape tunneling dynamics. At weak interaction, increasing $α$ drives a crossover from Josephson oscillations to dephasing and recurrent rephasing, demonstrating the importance of the interaction kernel's spatial structure. A higher barrier suppresses recurrences, whereas a larger initial imbalance promotes relaxation toward nearly vanishing population imbalance. Increasing interaction strength progressively suppresses population-transfer fluctuations, particularly at larger $α$. The two-mode extended Bose-Hubbard model captures the dynamics when the lowest orbital in each well dominates, but loses accuracy as additional orbitals become populated. In the strongly interacting regime, many-body spatial structures develop and several natural orbitals are needed for converged dynamics, placing the system beyond a two-mode description. Our results establish the interaction profile and strength, barrier, and initial state as distinct control parameters for coherent, dephasing, recurrent, and suppressed many-body tunneling of one-dimensional bosons. The ability to tailor soft-core interactions via Rydberg dressing offers a promising route to exploring interaction-engineered tunneling in ultracold atoms.

entry.title: Ultraviolet Structure of the Gravitational-Wave Response in a Time-Dependent Scalar Medium
entry.summary: We study the real-time linear response of gravitational waves in an FLRW background with a scalar field of general time-dependent effective mass. In the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we develop an adiabatic regularization scheme for unequal-time correlation functions and use it to extract the ultraviolet structure of the one-loop response. The leading divergence reproduces the familiar $\Box ^2h_{ij}$ structure, whereas the time-dependent background induces additional local divergences proportional to $\Box h_{ij}$, $\partial_τh_{ij}$, and $h_{ij}$. These are renormalized by local counterterms associated with the Weyl-squared term, a time-dependent Ricci-scalar term, a time-dependent cosmological constant, and the Ricci-scalar-squared term $R^2$. The same counterterms also remove the ultraviolet divergences of the background tadpole stress tensor and agree with the known covariant counterterm results. In a flat-background Mathieu oscillator example, replacing the adiabatic vacuum by the instantaneous vacuum leaves these counterterms unchanged but introduces an initial-surface divergence, which is absorbed into the initial data rather than the bulk counterterms.

entry.title: Quantum geometric ferromagnetism by singular saddle point
entry.summary: We propose ferromagnetism that occurs in electrons at a saddle point with band touching, which we call the singular saddle point. At the singular saddle point, the divergent quantum metric induces ferromagnetic correlation, and the logarithmic divergence of the density of states ensures ferromagnetism within Stoner theory. This is a prototypical example of quantum geometric ferromagnetism. The two-dimensional $t_{2g}$-orbital model accommodates the ferromagnetism by this mechanism, which is continuously connected to the exactly proven flat-band ferromagnetism.

entry.title: Cumulant dynamics of the ferromagnetic dipolar XY model
entry.summary: We study the second-order truncated cumulant dynamics for the preparation of dynamical states in the dipolar ferromagnetic XY model on the square lattice for system sizes up to linear size L = 60. The observations lead to a transparent picture in which a coherent region of finite extent and finite magnetization forms, which is possible even for diabatic but sufficiently slow ramps. These two scales are functions of the ramp constant, the initial entropy of the system, and time. Our findings put strong requirements on future experiments addressing dipolar XY equilibrium physics in bigger system sizes.

entry.title: Holographic dual of the 2d Ising model
entry.summary: We propose a holographic dual of the 2d Ising model on a torus as the Turaev-Viro TQFT on a solid torus. The bulk spacetime is divided into the ``core'' region and the ``sandwich'' region. The core region prepares a defect state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on the topological boundary $\mathbb{D}$. The sandwich region computes the Turaev-Viro state sum $\langle\mathcal{D}|Π|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ between the state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and the state $|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ on the physical boundary $\mathbb{B}$. The fusion diagram (or string-net) $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{B}$ is given by the Aasen-Fendley-Mong construction. There is also a ``bedding surface'' $\mathbb{S}$ between $\mathbb{D}$ and $\mathbb{B}$, and the height variables (or Ising spins inside/outside of the domain wall) are naturally living on $\mathbb{S}$. The bulk spacetime is discretized by the 2-skeleton $P$ which interpolates $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{F}$. When the defect $\mathcal{D}$ is absent, the 2-skeleton $P$ ends on the bedding surface $\mathbb{S}$ and $P$ is interpreted as the bulk worldsheet of the string-net $\mathcal{F}$.

entry.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
entry.summary: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.

entry.title: LHAASO's Peanut source is a laboratory for studying magnetic fields in the Milky Way
entry.summary: Recently, the LHAASO Collaboration reported gamma-ray emission from the Peanut-shaped source (Peanut), which extends over $4.5^\circ$ parallel to the Galactic plane at $b=-17.5^\circ$. The source is associated with the millisecond pulsar PSR J0218+4232, located at the eastern edge of the Peanut, at a distance of 3 kpc from the Earth and 0.9 kpc from the Galactic plane. Its location and bright gamma-ray emission above 25 TeV make it a natural laboratory for studying the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) in the transition region between the Galactic plane and halo. We interpret the observed emission as inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by electrons propagating along the large-scale GMF, accounting for turbulence through two models: Kolmogorov and Goldreich-Sridhar (GS). These models correspond to diffusive and ballistic particle propagation, respectively. While the GS case naturally provides conditions for one-sided gamma-ray emission, in the Kolmogorov case assumptions of one-sided particle injection and magnetic mirror at the source are necessary. We find that, in the Kolmogorov scenario, the Peanut's hotspots are likely associated with magnetic bottling, whereas in the GS scenario, they are related to magnetic field line geometry. Both models yield constraints on the GMF at the location of the Peanut.

entry.title: From $3\times2$pt to $4\times3$pt: calibrating galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments with galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra
entry.summary: Combining galaxy clustering and weak gravitational lensing beyond two-point statistics offers a way to extract additional cosmological information while calibrating astrophysical nuisance parameters. We investigate this approach by combining 1-loop power spectra with tree-level bispectra, including all auto- and cross-bispectra of galaxy clustering and weak lensing, a combination that we refer to as $4\times3$pt by analogy with the well-known $3\times2$pt analysis. Modelling two- and three-point statistics consistently, with galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments described by the TATT model, we perform Fisher forecasts of dark energy constraints for a Euclid-like survey, with conservative scale cuts. When combined with CMB data, adding $4\times3$pt bispectra to the $3\times2$pt improves the dark energy figure of merit by about $30\%$, a gain that remains stable when using the three, four or five lowest redshift bins of our ten. To extend the analysis to ten tomographic bins, we compress the bispectra into skew-spectra, which improve the figure of merit by $20\%$ with the CMB and by $37\%$ without. We show that most of this improvement comes from the calibration of second-order galaxy bias parameters by three-point statistics, mainly by the galaxy-auto and the GGL bispectra. We also find that baryonic feedback is correlated with second-order intrinsic alignment parameters once the amplitude of the matter power spectrum is constrained by the CMB, and that bispectra reduce this correlation by calibrating intrinsic alignments, almost entirely through the GGL bispectra, a mechanism that could become more valuable with more flexible baryonic feedback models. These results demonstrate the potential of combined galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra to improve cosmological constraints from stage-IV galaxy surveys through the calibration of galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments.

entry.title: Numerical Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes with Higher-Order Mass Corrections
entry.summary: Inspired by noncommutative geometry and quintessence, we construct a new class of asymptotically anti-de Sitter black hole solutions characterized by a higher-order mass deformation term $\frac{aM^{n-1}}{r^n}$ involving two parameters, $a$ and $n$. Due to analytical difficulties, we approach the underlying thermodynamics through parallel programming simulations using CUDA codes. By considering models with $n=3$, $n=4$, and $n=5$, we numerically study certain thermodynamic properties, including the stability, the $P$-$v$ criticality, and the phase transitions.

entry.title: Radiation from scattering on multiple shockwaves
entry.summary: It is well known that radiation produced by scattering an electron off multiple sources depends on the length of the mean free path between these scatterings. When this is sufficiently small, the spectrum is suppressed due to destructive interference, a famous result known as the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. This is usually modelled approximately, with scattering centres treated linearly (e.g., as screened Coulomb potentials), high-energy probes and soft emitted photons. In this paper, we consider a scenario where multiple scatterings can be computed exactly: charged probe scattering on multiple null electromagnetic shockwaves. Here, the amplitudes for elastic scattering and single photon emission can be determined exactly, for arbitrary kinematics, in terms of the shock profiles in the transverse plane. We use these amplitudes to compute the radiation density (doubly-averaged over shock locations in the transverse plane and lightfront time) in the regimes of independent and interfering scatterings. For shock profiles which are radially symmetric in the transverse plane (including the ultraboosted Coulomb field), we recover the known LPM suppression, albeit with more general kinematics. In addition, our setup allows us to consider the source-free case of multiple scattering on impulsive/ultra-short plane waves, where we find much stronger suppression of the spectrum in the LPM regime.

entry.title: Origin of the Fe K$α$ red excess in IC 4329A with XRISM and multi-wavelength spectroscopy
entry.summary: We present high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy of the bright local Seyfert 1 galaxy IC 4329A obtained with \textit{XRISM}/Resolve, supported by simultaneous \textit{NuSTAR} data and quasi-simultaneous optical/near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. Resolve separates the Fe K$α$ line into a narrow core and a broad component exhibiting a red excess. We examined three scenarios for this red excess: (1) a redshifted X-ray broad line region (xBLR), (2) relativistic disk reflection, and (3) an unshifted xBLR partially absorbed by a mildly ionized absorber. All three models reproduce the X-ray spectra equally well. Our optical (H$β$) and NIR (Pa$β$) spectroscopy shows that the broad lines are redshifted by $v \sim +640\text{--}1050\text{ km s}^{-1}$, close to the solution of the redshifted xBLR model ($v_{\rm shift} = +1700_{-800}^{+1700}\text{ km s}^{-1}$). Motivated by this, we constructed a hybrid model in which the xBLR shares the velocity structure of the optical/NIR BLR and the remaining red excess is attributed to a relativistic disk line, which also provides an acceptable fit. The inferred xBLR radius is $R_{\rm BLR} \sim (3\text{--}6) \times 10^3\ R_g$ ($\sim 12\text{--}22$ light-days). From the narrow Fe K$α$ core in the hybrid model (${\rm FWHM} = 870_{-280}^{+260}\text{ km s}^{-1}$), we estimate a torus distance of $R_{\rm torus} \sim 0.9_{-0.4}^{+1.0}$ pc ($\sim 1100$ light-days), close to the dust sublimation radius. Furthermore, two ultra-fast outflow (UFO) absorption features are identified with $v_{\text{wind}} \sim -0.30c$ and $-0.24c$, both confirmed at $>99\%$ confidence.

entry.title: Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn
entry.summary: The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.

entry.title: On JT boundary algebras
entry.summary: We construct the canonical boundary algebras of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter. For a nonempty finite or countable family of species with lowest weights greater than one half, the two boundary algebras are mutual commutants and nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ factors. Their nonzero finite corners are nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. The construction uses bounded heat-regularized fields and a Hilbert algebra, which gives a faithful normal semifinite trace without a path-integral argument. The weight restriction is sharp: elementary point fields remain unbounded after positive heat regularization when $0<d\leq1/2$. For one massless scalar, specified bounded observables and normal states have a high energy limit described by a hyperfinite continuous core. We explain why this limit does not preserve the nonhyperfiniteness of the exact algebra.

entry.title: Multifractal collective order : Application to multifractal superconductivity in dodecagonal quasicrystals
entry.summary: Conventional descriptions of collective ordering often assume spatially uniform order parameters, although the underlying electronic states can exhibit strong spatial inhomogeneity or multifractality. Here, we demonstrate that deterministic aperiodic geometry can instead stabilize multifractal collective order. We formulate a general diagnostic applicable to superconducting, magnetic, and charge channels, combining direct scaling analysis of the order parameter with three criteria: its spatial hierarchy must be dictated by the underlying geometry, emerge in the leading ordering instability, and persist in the self-consistent ordered state below a single mean-field ordering onset. We demonstrate that superconductivity on the experimentally resolved Ti network of a dodecagonal oxide quasicrystal satisfies all three criteria. The resulting condensate exhibits multifractal scaling over the resolved range of spatial scales, retaining its hierarchical structure throughout the ordered phase and channeling flux-induced equilibrium currents along geometry-locked rings.

entry.title: Spectra and Central Charges of Gauged Curvature Squared Supergravities in Five Dimensions
entry.summary: We study the spectra and the central charges of off-shell gauged five-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supergravity extended by the Weyl squared, Ricci tensor squared and Ricci scalar squared invariants, and by their Gauss-Bonnet combination. Working exactly in the couplings and keeping all auxiliary fields, we organize the spectra around the maximally supersymmetric AdS$_5$ vacuum into supermultiplets. With the Ricci scalar squared invariant, the spectrum gains a long vector multiplet and is free of ghosts in a finite range of the coupling, while with the Weyl squared or Ricci tensor squared invariant, it gains a long spin-2 multiplet and always contains ghosts or instabilities. The Gauss-Bonnet combination adds no new modes: around its supersymmetric vacuum, the quadratic action is a rescaled copy of that of the two-derivative theory, and this fixes the spectrum of the Ricci tensor squared extension. We also compute the central charges $a$ and $c$ and the flavor central charge exactly in the couplings. The vacuum equation is $a$-maximization, and the kinetic terms of the massless graviton and vector multiplets are proportional to $c$ and to the flavor central charge, so that the critical points, where the massive spin-2 multiplet becomes degenerate with the graviton multiplet, are zeros of $c$. Finally, around supersymmetric AdS$_3\timesΣ_2$ backgrounds of the Gauss-Bonnet extension, the two-dimensional central charges are reproduced by $c$-extremization, while the spectrum is generically not unitary and contains towers of states whose energies stay bounded at large Kaluza-Klein levels. In part of the parameter space, the tower of spin-2 multiplets has positive norm, so that the spectrum has no finite density of states.

entry.title: Kerr-NUT Thermodynamics: Misner Strings and Nut Charges
entry.summary: Using the thermodynamic approach introduced in e-Print: 2206.09124 [hep-th] to the case of Kerr-NUT solution, we demonstrate the existence of a new conserved quantity that is dual to the angular momentum, in the same way that the nut charge "n" is dual to the mass "m". This quantity exists regardless of the presence of the Kerr rotation parameter $a$, but only affects its thermodynamics when $a\neq 0$. The thermodynamic quantities calculated together with the two charges $N_{c}=cn$ and $N_{n}=n$ lead to consistent thermodynamic relations. That is, the first law, Smarr's and Gibbs-Duhem relations are all satisfied.

entry.title: A ménage à quatre without strings attached
entry.summary: When two D-branes with eight mixed Dirichlet-Neumann directions cross, a fundamental string is created. This is the Hanany-Witten (HW) effect. In supergravity, the string shows up as an electric NSNS B-field sourced by the RR fields of the two branes. We show that two brane pairs, each of which would create an HW string on its own, can combine into a quadruple bound state with no HW strings attached. We explicitly construct a background with the fluxes of such a D0-D8-D4-D4' quadruple. Requiring no HW strings imposes a quadratic relation among the fluxes. We also realize this bound state as a supersymmetric solution of the non-Abelian DBI action of the D8-branes, whose Killing spinors match those of the bulk supergravity solution. The fluxed D8 stack acts as a domain wall between two supersymmetric D0-D8-D4-D4' backgrounds. Each background satisfies the no-string constraint, and the jumps in the fluxes give the charges carried by the stack.

entry.title: D(-1)/D7 bound states in supergravity
entry.summary: We construct D($-$1)/D7 bound states in Euclidean type IIB supergravity motivated by the string-theory setup of Billò et al., whose open-string description realizes instantons in eight-dimensional super Yang--Mills theory. Previous supergravity constructions either left unresolved issues concerning ten-dimensional Euclidean supersymmetry or relied on partial smearing to codimension one. We classify the local codimension-two solutions by showing that the supersymmetric field equations reduce to two holomorphic functions subject to a single complex constraint. The candidate bound-state solutions require complementary D3-brane fluxes, consistent with the D7 worldvolume analysis. A particularly interesting solution has constant dilaton and connects the vacuum at infinity to a controlled scaling limit in which the geometry becomes $\mathbb R\times S^1\times\mathbb T^8$.

entry.title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
entry.summary: Monodromy line defects arise as boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, providing a natural route to conformal defects with implications in condensed matter, gauge theories and quantum information. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we realize monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $Z_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), the $π$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT, and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $π$-twist and reflection). For each defect we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the critical bulk. Among the resolved low-lying defect primaries we find no relevant scalar perturbation preserving all symmetries of the corresponding defect; the relevant deformations identified break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. For the partial twists of O(3), we derive the flow of the symmetry-preserving untwisted zero-mode mass generated by the bulk interaction. Its weak-coupling runaway near four dimensions motivates a careful distinction between the microscopic absence of pinning, the free reference background, and a possible infrared defect fixed point in three dimensions. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist, turning the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization for exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.

entry.title: Exact model of a gravitational wave and electromagnetic radiation in DHOST gravity theory: wave solutions and testable effects
entry.summary: Within an analytical non-perturbative framework based on a single exact model, the coupled dynamics of gravitational waves and high-frequency electromagnetic fields is investigated in General Relativity and DHOST gravity. Using an exact gravitational-wave spacetime in an isotropic (null) wave coordinate system, Maxwell's equations are integrated analytically. This analysis provides an exact non-perturbative confirmation from the full field equations that a gravitational wave acts as a waveguide, forming a propagation channel for electromagnetic radiation co-directional with the gravitational wave and generating an effective pure-radiation source. Applying this exact electrodynamic solution to the nonlinear field equations of DHOST class~Ia gravity reveals that the algebraic structure of the DHOST constraint equations enforces a modification of the electromagnetic-wave parameters. Based on this mechanism, an observationally testable effect of scalar frequency drift is derived, providing a direct way to discriminate between General Relativity and modified gravity theories even when their metric tensors share identical functional forms.

entry.title: Accessing Continuous Monodromy Defects of the 3D Conformal Field Theory on the Fuzzy Sphere
entry.summary: Monodromy defects are line defects at the boundary of a topological symmetry surface, around which charged operators acquire a symmetry phase. They probe how a critical system responds to an inserted symmetry flux, but their universal information at strongly coupled fixed points, in particular for a continuous family of twists, remains hard to access. Here we investigate the continuous family of $U(1)$ monodromy defect with fractional twist angles embedded in the three-dimensional $O(2)$ Wilson--Fisher conformal field theory. We realize this continuous family of defects within the fuzzy-sphere framework by threading a fractional Aharonov--Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We observe charged defect operators carrying fractional transverse spins, as a characteristic signature of the imposed monodromy, and a displacement operator close to its protected dimension, supporting the conformal nature of the defect line. Crucially, we resolve no relevant symmetry-preserving scalar, and identify the charge-one defect operators as the only relevant, symmetry-breaking deformations. Assuming the particle--vortex duality, the U(1) monodromy defect maps to a Wilson line of fractional charge in the critical noncompact Abelian Higgs model, and our results then provide evidence that these Wilson lines with fractional charge are locally stable conformal lines.

entry.title: Going beyond the standard quasiparticle picture: Entanglement spreading after quenching from highly entangled states
entry.summary: The quasiparticle picture provides a quantitative description of entanglement spreading after quantum quenches in integrable systems. In interacting models, however, it relies on the assumption that the quench creates entangled pairs of quasiparticles, which is justified only for the so-called integrable initial states. Here we go beyond this setting by studying quenches in the XXZ spin chain from the $n$-rainbow states, a family of macroscopically homogeneous states formed by increasingly long-range Bell pairs, which are not integrable for $n>1$. The local stationary state after the quench approaches the infinite-temperature state as $n\to\infty$, with corrections of order $1/n$, as we show analytically. Nevertheless, in the noninteracting XX chain the quench produces entangled multiplets of $2n$ species of quasiparticles. Although interspecies correlations vanish as $1/n$, they strongly suppress the growth of the entanglement entropy, whose rate vanishes as $n\to\infty$. We capture this behaviour within a generalized quasiparticle picture. In the interacting XXZ chain, instead, time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (tDMRG) simulations show that the entanglement entropy grows at the rate at which thermodynamic entropy is exchanged across the cut. Within the time scales accessible to tDMRG, the data show no trace of the multiplet suppression. This holds both after homogeneous quenches and after joining the $n$-rainbow state with an infinite-temperature state, for which we conjecture a formula for the von Neumann entropy.

entry.title: Maximal force bounds in general relativity and beyond
entry.summary: Gibbons and Schiller proposed the maximal force conjecture in general relativity, according to which the maximum force is bounded by $c^4/G$. In this work, we derive upper bounds on the force for stable, self-gravitating, spatially regular and horizonless compact objects in $d$-dimensional general relativity, braneworld gravity, pure Lovelock gravity and Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Our analysis uses the connection between photon-ring structure and the stability of horizonless compact objects, adopting the absence of light rings as a criterion for stability. We investigate how the resulting force bounds depend on the spacetime dimension and on modifications to gravitational dynamics arising from extra dimensions and higher curvature corrections. We study how the bounds for such systems change under alternative higher curvature theories of gravity or in higher dimensions. Throughout this work, we consider a static and spherically symmetric spacetime sourced by anisotropic matter for which the radial and tangential pressures may differ.

entry.title: $r$-Largest Order Statistics for Galaxy Cluster Cosmology I: Reconstruction of the high-mass end of the Halo Mass Function
entry.summary: We introduce the $r$-largest order statistics ($r$-LOS) framework for galaxy clusters, a generalization of the standard extreme value statistics (EVS) approach. While conventional EVS focuses on the probability distribution of the most massive cluster within a given volume, the $r$-LOS framework exploits the additional statistical information encoded in the joint distribution of the $r$ most massive clusters, ranked in descending order of mass. We develop the corresponding mathematical formalism, discuss its asymptotic properties, and derive a set of relations relevant to galaxy cluster cosmology. In particular, we demonstrate that the high-mass end of the halo mass function (HMF) can be reconstructed from the generalized extreme value (GEV) parameters inferred using an extension of the block maxima method that incorporates the $r$ most massive clusters in each volume. This provides a means of recovering the high-mass tail of the HMF using only a small subsample of the halo population. We validate these relations using both comoving and light-cone halo catalogues from numerical simulations. Finally, we investigate the sensitivity of the $r$-LOS framework to primordial non-Gaussianity, focusing on its impact on the statistics of massive clusters.

entry.title: Energetic Particle Confinement In Black Hole Accretion Disks
entry.summary: Using tracer particles propagating in the environment provided by general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, this paper addresses fundamental questions related to the confinement and acceleration properties in accretion disks around compact objects. By varying the spin parameter of the central black hole and the accretion regime of the disk, a comprehensive picture is obtained for particles whose Larmor radius is comparable to the gravitational radius of the system. It is found that such particles can escape the system at the outermost boundary of the simulations, though, depending on the accretion regime, the time it takes them to escape, and the energetic dynamics along the trajectory can vary significantly. Dynamics near the black hole are even more sensitive to environmental details as black holes with higher spin values generate stronger magnetic fields, which influence particle motion in non-trivial ways. The primary acceleration mechanism is identified as turbulent scattering, with the jet-sheath emerging as the dominant site for particle energization

entry.title: Unconventional Pressure Evolution of Spin-Density-Wave State in La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$
entry.summary: The discovery of pressure-induced high temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ has raised the question of how its spin-density-wave (SDW) state evolves toward the superconducting regime. Here, we report a systematic electronic Raman study of La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ single crystals under hydrostatic pressures up to 16.51~GPa. Both the SDW gap energy and the transition temperature $T_{\mathrm{SDW}}$ show an overall increase with pressure, while the dimensionless coupling ratio $2Δ_{\mathrm{SDW}}/(k_{\mathrm B}T_{\mathrm{SDW}})$ remains approximately pressure independent, indicating a robust strong-coupling character of SDW state. At the same time, the SDW-related Raman peak broadens as pressure is applied, indicating the enhanced damping of the associated electronic excitation. These results reveal an unusual pressure evolution in which the SDW energy scale is enhanced while the SDW state becomes progressively less coherent, providing spectroscopic constraints on the magnetic correlations relevant to superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.

entry.title: Observational Tests for Distinguishing Classes of Cosmological Models
entry.summary: We investigate observational tests that can be used to distinguish between broad classes of cosmological models. This is achieved using curvature-consistency tests of the Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) models, which we investigate in two scenarios where they can be violated; (i) when the optical properties of the cosmology deviate from the expectations of FLRW, and also (ii) when the large-scale expansion of the cosmology is different from FLRW. We identify useful ways to determine the properties of these alternative scenarios in terms of the violation of the curvature-consistency tests, and propose a new null test that can be used to isolate cosmologies with non-FLRW observational relations. The characteristic signatures we find can be used, together with the results of recent and upcoming cosmological observations, to probe and/or rule out large classes of cosmological models. This becomes an increasingly important task as the number of proposals in the literature increases, as cosmologists attempt to explain tensions, anomalies, and the dark sector of the Universe. Our approach provides a clear route for telling apart these different proposals, and offers a new opportunity for using precision cosmological data to efficiently discriminate between cosmological models.

entry.title: A unified mean-field description of dense hadron matter constrained from $χ$EFT and lattice QCD
entry.summary: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.

entry.title: What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?
entry.summary: We explore the origin of an initial broad luminosity peak that precedes the light curve plateau in type IIP supernovae. It is well known that the explosion of an evolutionary red supergiant model in the frame of radiation hydrodynamics fails to reproduce the initial luminosity peak. A common practice to compensate this drawback is to introduce massive (> 0.3 Msun) circumstellar shell attached to the evolutionary model. This remedy, however, has a negative side effect - a strong deceleration of the outer ejecta, which is inconsistent with early spectral data. An alternative way out suggests modification of a hydrogen envelope of the evolutionary red supergiant model - the outer layers should have steeper density gradient. We perform the search for the optimal multi-parameter hydrodynamic model of type IIP SN 1999em based on the Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. The major result is that the initial luminous peak is well reproduced by the explosion of the red supergiant with the logarithmic density gradient smaller than -3 in the outer layers of about 0.9 Msun. We suggest that the mechanism for the density steepening in the hydrogen envelope is closely related to the unknown mechanism responsible for the creation of the ubiquitous low-mass (< 0.01 Msun) dense confined shell detected in type IIP supernovae.

entry.title: Six-Loop Renormalization in Quantum Electrodynamics
entry.summary: We analytically compute the six-loop corrections to the scale evolution of the electric charge, fermion mass, and fermion field in quantum electrodynamics. The results are obtained in the $\MSbar$ scheme for an arbitrary number of equally charged fermions. They extend renormalization in quantum electrodynamics by one loop order and allow new tests of the behavior of perturbation theory at high orders. The methods developed here also open the way to six-loop computations of renormalization in quantum chromodynamics.

entry.title: Interplay of Pair Density Wave and Uniform Superconductivity on the Kagome Lattice
entry.summary: We study the interplay between pair density wave (PDW) and uniform superconductivity on the kagome lattice within a single-orbital $t$-$W$-$J$ model near the $p$-type van Hove filling, where $W$ and $J$ denote effective pairing attractions on lattice sites and nearest-neighbor bonds, respectively. While onsite attraction favors zero-momentum pairing through the conventional BCS instability, nearest-neighbor attraction naturally promotes finite-momentum pairing due to the kagome geometry and sublattice interference. The model therefore provides a framework for exploring the competition and coexistence between uniform superconductivity and PDW order. Self-consistent mean-field calculations in a $2\times2$ supercell reveal that the uniform component reorganizes both the amplitudes and phase structure of the three $F_1$ PDW components, giving rise to superconducting states absent in the pure bond-pairing limit. A Ginzburg--Landau analysis identifies symmetry-allowed couplings that can favor this reorganization. The resulting states exhibit distinct charge modulations and quasiparticle spectra, while the chiral PDW undergoes topological transitions as the onsite attraction increases. Our results demonstrate how uniform superconductivity reshapes the order-parameter landscape and quasiparticle topology of a PDW state.

entry.title: Quasinormal modes and tidal responses of black holes in generic anisotropic matter environments
entry.summary: We develop a perturbative framework for a black hole embedded in a generic, possibly anisotropic, matter environment under spherical symmetry. Our approach extends previous analyses restricted to vanishing radial pressure or to perturbative matter configurations. Within this framework, we derive an analytical generalization of the Einstein cluster that incorporates a polytropic radial pressure, and we investigate the properties of this solution. We show that both the geodesic structure and the axial quasinormal-mode spectrum remain predominantly governed by an overall gravitational redshift effect, while the radial pressure systematically enhances the environmental corrections. In contrast, the tidal Love numbers are substantially more sensitive, and can exhibit order-unity deviations, including vanishing and negative strictly static magnetic Love numbers for sufficiently large anisotropy. We present the full linearized equations, which can be applied to various extensions, including ringdown analysis and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.

entry.title: Statistical properties of quadrangular surfaces
entry.summary: We investigate the statistical properties of random quadrangular surfaces generated by different randomization procedures: the Gruzberg-Klümper-Nuding-Sedrakyan (GKNS) construction, and two newly introduced generalizations of dynamical triangulations (DT), dynamical (DQ) and general quadrangulations (GQ). We formulate these surfaces within a unified graph-theoretic framework and establish the relationships between the elementary operations defining the different ensembles. For GKNS surfaces, we demonstrate that the construction is equivalent to two mutually constrained percolation processes and determine the associated critical point and critical exponents, revealing deviations from ordinary percolation. For DQ and GQ, we analyze the underlying Markov chains and determine the scaling of mixing and relaxation times. We further analyze all three ensembles through their degree distributions, degree correlations, distance statistics, and Hausdorff dimensions. While DQ exhibits exponentially decaying degree distributions and geometric properties similar to DT, GKNS and GQ display broad, scale-free degree distributions. Moreover, GKNS surfaces possess an asymptotic Hausdorff dimension $Δ_H\approx 2$, whereas DQ and GQ approach $Δ_H\approx 4$, similarly to DT. This indicates that DQ is compatible with the universal behavior of DT, while GKNS and GQ define distinct classes of random geometry, implying a different underlying measure in the space of random surfaces and a possible geometric framework for a new class of noncritical string theories.

entry.title: Magnetically Deformed Neutron Stars and Gravitational Waves
entry.summary: We study the geometric figures of neutron stars and magnetars with spin periods from milliseconds to seconds and magnetic fields from $10^{12}$-$10^{15}$ G to hypothetical values near the Chandrasekhar-Fermi virial scale, $10^{18}$ G. In Newtonian theory, we find the equilibrium figure of a rotating incompressible fluid with a current-free uniform interior magnetic field matched to an exterior dipole field by surface currents. For aligned axes, an oblate spheroid is obtained by minimizing the total gravitational, rotational and magnetic energy at fixed mass, volume, angular momentum and frozen magnetic flux. Its ellipticity is the sum of rotational and magnetic contributions, recovers the Ferraro limit for a weak magnetic field, and has a magnetic weight that depends on the eccentricity for large deformation. For misaligned magnetic and spin axes, we introduce a quadrupolar shape tensor and diagonalize it to find a triaxial ellipsoid whose principal axes are tilted by magnetic pressure. The tilt angle and eccentricities are computed analytically as functions of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities and the misalignment angle. The magnetic energy of the misaligned configuration is obtained in closed form in oblate spheroidal harmonics for arbitrary eccentricity and obliquity. Its weak-field deformation, up to $10^{15}$ G, is proportional to $P_2(\cosα)$, which fixes the magnetic forcing tensor, and its finite-eccentricity form gives a generalized Ferraro-Maclaurin relation for rotation-dominated misaligned stars. In the weak-field regime, the triaxial eccentricity is determined by the Ferraro eccentricity and the harmonic mean of order 2 of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities. The deformation parameters give the quadrupole moments and hence the continuous gravitational-wave amplitudes, luminosity and spin-down torque of the triaxial configuration.

entry.title: Discrete Supernovae and the Limits of Continuous Models in Low-Mass Dark Matter Halos
entry.summary: Many galaxy formation models represent supernova feedback by a continuous energy injection rate averaged over the stellar initial mass function (IMF). This approximation can fail in low-mass dark matter halos, where single, discrete supernovae can unbind more gas than the reservoir holds. We investigate this using a one-zone model that characterises continuous and discrete supernova feedback at redshifts $z\geq5$. Both feedback modes inject the same expected energy per unit stellar mass formed. In the discrete model, individual supernovae are resolved and energy is injected instantaneously; in the continuous model, supernovae are IMF-averaged and energy injection is spread over a finite time interval. Once stars form, a supernova can unbind 1.5-2.7 times the gas present. Continuous feedback begins removing gas after $\sim 4$ Myr, whereas the first discrete supernova occurs after $\sim 10$ Myr, which produces a stellar mass excess before feedback takes effect. The excess persists because the reservoir responds nonlinearly: an event removes at most the gas present, and star formation halts once it is empty. It depends strongly on halo mass: from 135 per cent at $10^7\, \rm{M}_\odot$, to 15 per cent at $10^8\, \rm{M}_\odot$, to negligible at $10^9\, \rm{M}_\odot$ by $z=5$. Fixing the number and timing of supernovae does not remove the stellar excess, which indicates that it is not caused by stochastic IMF sampling. Instead, it vanishes when the same energy is divided among more, smaller events. Matching the energy released per unit stellar mass therefore does not guarantee equivalent feedback in halos that retain gas until the first supernova.

entry.title: FOORT: Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing
entry.summary: We present FOORT (Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing), an open C++ code for ray-tracing images of black holes and other compact objects in arbitrary spacetimes. FOORT is designed to offer flexibility and can handle horizons, naked singularities and numerical metrics, allowing it to ray-trace numerous different metrics including Kerr and other black holes, as well as horizonless objects such as fuzzballs and boson stars. New metrics, analytical or numerical, can be added with minimal effort, and geodesics are initialized at the camera without reference to conserved quantities, so no special structure of the metric is required. Besides the intensity observed from a geometrically and optically thin equatorial disk, FOORT is set up to track a number of diagnostics along each geodesic, such as the number of equatorial crossings and the radius of closest approach. Its adaptive mesh can refine the image on any of these diagnostics, efficiently resolving narrow features such as higher-order photon rings. Accompanying Python tools convert the output into images and interferometric visibility amplitudes. We describe the main features of the code, validate it against analytic results in the Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, demonstrate it on several non-Kerr metrics, and characterize its scaling with the number of OpenMP threads. FOORT is lightweight, requiring only C++17 and OpenMP, and has already been used in a number of studies of black hole and compact-object imaging. The code is publicly available in a GitHub repository.

entry.title: Homotopies in Batalin-Vilkovisky Formalism
entry.summary: We review the notion of homotopy of quantum master actions in geometric Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. Then we construct new examples of such homotopies, coming from renormalization group flow and non-infinitesimal changes of gauge fixing. Finally, we use the field redefinitions given by these homotopies to construct spans of quantum master actions with isomorphic effective actions.

entry.title: Conserved gravitational-wave Stress-Energy Tensor in General Metric Theories
entry.summary: We construct a gravitational-wave (GW) stress-energy tensor for general metric theories and show that it is conserved after averaging in the wave zone. In metric theories involving a vector field, we find that the conventional GW stress-energy tensor is generally not conserved. Combining the diffeomorphism identity, we identify the vector-field contribution required in addition to the conventional GW stress-energy tensor. On this basis, in a flat vacuum wave zone with constant background fields and after short-wavelength averaging, the perturbed field equation, perturbed action, Landau-Lifshitz, and Noether current methods yield equivalent tensors. In this setting, the completed tensor is generally nonsymmetric and satisfies $\partial_μτ^{μν}=0$, with energy flux $cτ^{i0}$. It also does not depend on whether a covariant or contravariant vector is chosen as the fundamental variable. Applying this framework to Einstein-æther theory, we derive the orbital energy losses of an adiabatic quasicircular compact binary, and provide a possible explanation for the discrepancies among previous results in this theory. These results establish a consistent radiation balance that allows additional gravitational degrees of freedom to be connected to the evolution of astrophysical systems and to observational tests of gravity.

entry.title: Weak null singularities for the Einstein--Vlasov system
entry.summary: We study the formation and stability of weak null singularities for solutions to the massive and massless Einstein--Vlasov systems without symmetry assumptions. Extending previous results of Luk in the vacuum setting, we establish the existence of spacetimes arising from characteristic initial data that develop a singular null boundary while remaining extendible with a continuous metric. For both massive and massless particles, the energy-momentum tensor and Ricci curvature remain bounded and extend continuously to the singular boundary. For genuinely singular initial data, the Christoffel symbols in the original double-null coordinates fail to be locally square integrable near the boundary. We introduce new commutator vector fields that avoid both derivative loss and the most singular curvature component. Under additional curvature assumptions, we also prove Lipschitz inextendibility across the singular null boundary.

entry.title: Magnetars magnetic field evolution with ambipolar diffusion
entry.summary: The magnetic field associated with neutron stars is generally believed to be threaded inside the star. In the presence of a magnetic field, plasma in the interior of the star undergoes a series of processes that result in magnetic field evolution. It is believed that magnetar activities like X-ray, gamma-ray bursts, and giant flares (which release more energy in a few sec than Sun in 10 years), are mainly due to field decay. The most important process of field decay inside the core of the star is the ambipolar diffusion of the charged particles present in the interior plasma. The decay rate due to ambipolar diffusion is directly connected to the ambipolar velocity of the charged particles under the influence of the present magnetic field. The ambipolar velocity of the charged particles depends on the internal dynamics of the particles. We outline a general method to solve the particle dynamics in the presence of a magnetic field to have a magnetohydrodynamics equation from ambipolar velocity. The equation is general and applicable to all possible surrounding conditions temperature, matter states like normal or superfluid, etc.

entry.title: Thermality from a Rindler quench
entry.summary: Ultracold fermionic atoms in an optical lattice, with a sudden position-dependent change (a quench) in the effective dispersion relation, have been proposed by Rodríguez-Laguna et al. as an analogue spacetime test of the Unruh effect. We provide new support for this analogue by analysing a massless scalar field on a $(1+1)$-dimensional continuum spacetime with a similar quench: an early time Minkowski region is joined at a constant time surface, representing the quench, to a late time static region in which left and right asymptotically Rindler domains are connected by a smooth negative curvature bridge. We show that the quench is energetically mild, and late time static observers, modelled as a derivative-coupling Unruh-DeWitt detector, see thermality, in a temperature that equals the Unruh temperature for observers in the asymptotic Rindler domains. The Unruh effect hence prevails, despite the energy injected into the field by the quench and despite the absence of a late time Killing horizon. These results strengthen the motivation to realise the experimental proposal.

entry.title: Constraining models of inflation via an asymptotic de Sitter realization of Bianchi cosmologies
entry.summary: Our Universe is isotropic and homogeneous when we observe it on $\gtrsim$ Mpc length scales. It is desirable that present state of the Universe has no dependence on its initial geometry. In case of Bianchi Universes, i.e., anisotropic but homogeneous Universe, this has already been demonstrated via cosmological constant in a process that we call \textit{de Sitterization}. In this letter, we show that for Bianchi Universe, the same state can be achieved by a homogeneous inflaton field with a general potential and satisfying a criterion without the need of a cosmological constant. More importantly, we show that the same condition can constrain models of inflation and explain our idea with examples.

entry.title: Anisotropic separate universe : Long-wavelength perturbations and conserved quantities
entry.summary: We study the superhorizon evolution of linear perturbations in an anisotropic Bianchi type I universe with a scalar field coupled to a U(1) gauge field. The analysis employs the spatial gradient expansion in the uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ gauge, in which the local number of $e$-folds is unperturbed. In this gauge, the complete set of leading-order long-wavelength solutions, including both even- and odd-parity perturbations, can be constructed from variations of homogeneous Bianchi type I solutions, subject to the momentum and Gauss constraints. The conserved Wronskian found in isotropic multi-field inflation is generalized to the anisotropic system. Together with the shear and electric-flux integration constants, it allows the curvature perturbation on uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ hypersurfaces to be expressed in terms of background variations and time integrals. The conserved comoving curvature perturbations are then obtained by adding this intrinsic curvature contribution to the familiar $δN$ contribution arising from the change of time slicing. We also derive a relation between the curvature perturbation and a metric perturbation that reduces to the plus-polarized tensor mode in the isotropic limit, and discuss a nonlinear extension of the formalism.

entry.title: Quasinormal Modes of a Black Hole in a Dehnen-Type Dark Matter Halo with Radial Pressure
entry.summary: We investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of scalar and (axial) gravitational perturbations of a black hole spacetime surrounded by a Dehnen-type dark matter (DM) halo with nonvanishing radial pressure. Our results reveal that the real and imaginary parts of the QNMs exhibit distinct redshift coefficients with respect to the DM halo compactness $M/a_0$, in contrast to the vanishing radial pressure case. The magnitude of this effect is dominated by the profile parameter $γ$, and the damping rate is more sensitive to the DM halo compactness than the oscillation frequency. In the eikonal limit, the redshift deviations are well captured by the light ring angular velocity $Ω_c$ and the Lyapunov exponent $λ$.

entry.title: On the MeV Nuclear De-excitation Line Emission from the Vela Supernova Remnant Region
entry.summary: We investigate the potential nuclear de-excitation $γ$-ray line emission from low-energy cosmic rays (LECRs) in the Vela SNR region, one of the nearest and most angularly extended core-collapse supernova remnant (SNR) complexes. We calculate the MeV line emission from Vela, Vela Jr., and Puppis A using the TALYS nuclear reaction code, considering both direct and inverse interactions between the accelerated particles and the nuclei interior to the SNRs. The proton spectra are constrained by GeV--TeV $γ$-ray observations under the hadronic assumption, while a broad range of spectral indices is explored to account for the poorly constrained LECR population. We find that Vela dominates the predicted line flux among the three SNRs. The integrated fluxes of the prominent 1.63 MeV $^{20}$Ne, 4.44 MeV $^{12}$C and 6.13 MeV $^{16}$O lines are approximately $1.3\times10^{-10}$ -- $1.2\times10^{-6}$, $3.2\times10^{-10}$ -- $5.6\times10^{-7}$ and $1.6\times10^{-10}$--$2.6\times10^{-7}$ $\rm ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}$, respectively, over the explored proton spectra. We compare the predicted line emission with both the diffuse Galactic MeV continuum and local source-related continuum emission. In our background estimate, diffuse Galactic emission is the dominant component, while inverse Compton emission from pulsar wind nebula Vela X constitutes an additional local continuum component. The relatively low diffuse background toward Vela compared with the Galactic Center makes this region a promising target for future MeV $γ$-ray observations. Such observations could provide direct constraints on the LECR population and particle acceleration in this complex SNR region.

entry.title: Enhancing Graviton--Photon Conversion through Galactic Magnetic Turbulence
entry.summary: Plasma dispersion suppresses coherent graviton-photon conversion over astrophysical distances. We show that Galactic magnetic turbulence enables phase matching by compensating the plasma-induced mismatch, allowing matched magnetic modes to contribute coherently. In the long path limit, the ensemble-averaged conversion probability grows linearly with propagation distance in the phase matched regime and is governed by the projected magnetic power spectrum. Applied to photon background observations, this mechanism yields characteristic strain limits that are stronger than previous Galactic conversion bounds in the inertial range phase matching window, with improvements of up to two orders of magnitude.

entry.title: A Non-local "Boundary" Term for Two-Point Amplitudes in String Field Theory
entry.summary: We propose a new ``boundary'' term in free bosonic string field theory. With the original choice of energy operators, the term is non-local in time. We construct this term as a bilinear form involving the commutator of the BRST operator with the step-function operator. The resulting action restores cyclicity, as required for a variational principle. When evaluated on on-shell string fields, the proposed term reproduces the correct tree-level two-point amplitude for both open and closed strings. We verify this explicitly in the tachyon and massless sectors. An alternative off-shell choice yields a time-local boundary term with the same on-shell amplitudes. For the open-string tachyon, this yields an initial-data prescription.

entry.title: Astrometric effects of anisotropic gravitational wave backgrounds
entry.summary: Precise astrometric observations of distant objects such as stars and quasars can be used to probe gravitational wave signals at nanohertz frequencies. A stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) produces correlated apparent motions of pairs of objects on the sky. That correlation as a function of their angular separation is the astrometric analog of the Hellings-Downs curve in the context of pulsar timing measurements. Upper limits on the SGWB have been obtained from very-long baseline interferometry and Gaia astrometry, and future Gaia data releases are expected to improve them. An astrophysical background from inspiraling supermassive black hole binaries is expected to be significantly anisotropic. In this work, we compute the astrometric correlation functions for an anisotropic SGWB, known as the generalized overlap reduction functions, for all six gravitational wave polarizations. We present closed-form expressions in all cases where the distant-light source limit can be applied, following the approach used for pulsar timing arrays. We find that the correlations differ qualitatively between the tensor, vector, and scalar polarizations. Finally, we discuss the applicability of these results in future astrometry searches for arbitrarily polarized anisotropic gravitational wave backgrounds.

entry.title: Topologically protected zero-reflection nodes for perfect crossed Andreev reflection
entry.summary: Generating non-locally entangled electron pairs via Cooper-pair splitting is vital for solid-state quantum information processing. However, isolating the underlying crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is challenging due to competing transport processes like electron tunneling (ET) and local Andreev reflection (AR). Here, we propose a flux-tunable four-terminal normal metal-superconductor junction that achieves deterministic, 100\% efficient CAR. We demonstrate that at exactly half a magnetic flux quantum ($φ=π$), exact destructive Aharonov-Bohm and Peierls interferences structurally forbid ET and AR, respectively. By tuning the central junction hopping, electron reflection is also suppressed to zero. Using the Cauchy argument principle, we prove that this zero-reflection node is topologically protected by a quantized winding number in parameter space. When combined with the precise spatial symmetries of the junction, this exact suppression guarantees a unit CAR probability. We establish that this regime is characterized by a strictly positive cross-correlation shot noise, providing an unambiguous experimental signature of Cooper-pair splitting. Furthermore, this perfect CAR is nearly broadband within the superconducting gap. While generic structural disorder breaks the spatial symmetries required for the exact cancellation of ET and AR, the crossed Andreev reflection--though no longer perfectly quantized --remains highly dominant under weak disorder, offering a resilient architecture for deterministic nonlocal entanglement generation.

entry.title: Flux Variation of the Crab Pulsar Observed Using Fermi LAT and NuSTAR
entry.summary: The flux of pulsed emission from the Crab pulsar, just like most of other pulsars, is considered to be steady over time scales much larger than the pulsation period, except for a smooth, secular decrease related to the aging of pulsars. Such a steady assumption prevails in all theoretical investigations of pulsar emission models. However, here we report the discovery of stochastic variation in the flux and photon index of the Crab pulsar gamma-ray and hard X-ray emissions utilizing archival data of Fermi LAT (0.1 -- 100 GeV, spanning 17 years) and of NuSTAR (3.0 -- 79.0 keV, spanning 13 years) observations. Furthermore, the flux variation is found to be anti-correlated with variation of the spectral photon index, that is, harder when brighter, in both gamma ray and hard X-ray bands. The origin of such variation is intriguing. Some possibilities are discussed.

entry.title: A general formula for the amplitude-frequency ratio in shaking induced Mott insulator of atomtronic transistors
entry.summary: Mott insulator of atomic transport can be realized in shaken optical lattices by choosing particular ratio of driving amplitude and frequency, which has been studied as Floquet engineering with time-independent effective Hamiltonian approach. Here, we give a general formula of amplitude-frequency ratio for realization of the shaking induced insulator-conductor transition in a double-well open system, using numerical computation with instantaneous eigenstates approach. The result is owing to the fact that the instantaneous eigenstates approach is applicable in wider parameter range compared with the time-independent effective Hamiltonian approach. Analysis from the results of quantum master equation shows that the insulator effect is originated from coherent localization of atom wave packets in optical wells.

entry.title: Periodic orbits and gravitational waveforms of spinning particles in nonlocal gravity
entry.summary: In this paper, we investigate the dynamics and gravitational-wave signatures of periodic orbits of spinning test particles moving in the equatorial plane around static, spherically symmetric black holes within the framework of Deser-Woodard nonlocal gravity. Based on the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations, combined with the Tulczyjew spin supplementary condition, we derive the orbital dynamic equations for spinning particles moving in the equatorial plane and impose a timelike constraint to exclude unphysical superluminal trajectories. By comparing with the classical Schwarzschild black hole, we systematically analyze the effects of the nonlocal gravitational parameters $ζ$ and $b$ on the effective potential governing the radial motion of particles and the innermost stable circular orbit. In addition, gravitational waveforms exhibit significant phase differences: an increase in $ζ$ induces a phase delay, whereas an increase in $b$ results in a phase advance. Using periodic-orbit waveforms extended over a one-year interval with fixed orbital parameters, we obtain an order-of-magnitude estimate of the sensitivity of the waveform mismatch to nonlocal corrections. For the configurations considered, this estimate suggests sensitivity to $ζ$ of order $10^{-6}$ when $b=2$.
